title: How the New Orleans bands differed from Chicago bands
summary: New Orleans drummers brought new rhythms, and ballads played in ragtime; Saints and Swanee River.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: No, that's right. That's what you think. I was going to ask about the New Orleans fellas when they first came up here. The bands like say Oliver. You heard Oliver and all of those. Yes. Did they seem much different than the Chicago bands? Well, yes.
Yeah, they brought something with them.
What was different? Did they have a different beat or a different melody or what kind of?

Yeah, they brought drummers here that made us all take notice. They played rhythms and things. The whole bunch and you know, and joined them. That played beats we'd never heard. They'd never been heard up this way. And couldn't change you know. In the different times. And then they brought all those ballads. They come up here playing all ballads in ragtime, jazz time. They started all that up here too.
The Swanee River. All of those.
And jazz. Not jazz, but ragtime. Yeah.
Do you remember some of the pieces you first heard them play, the New Orleans bands that played when they first hit town?

Yes, Saints was one of the best. One of the first good ones. I see they're imitating it now. You hear it on the radio now occasionally. Saints, Swanee River, Melancholy Baby, all of those kind of tunes. We'd been playing them. We never played them in no ragtime. Not like they did.
